title: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Salary: The Karl Stefanovic Salary Example
description: Wondering about the karl stefanovic salary? Learn how to convert hourly rates to annual pay, including casual loading and super, using the national minimum wage and award rates.
salarySummary: For a standard 38-hour week, annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52. Casual loading adds 25% on top, and super is paid on top of that.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect my hourly rate?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% on top of the base hourly rate, intended to compensate for the lack of paid leave. For example, the national minimum wage of $26.44 per hour becomes $33.05 per hour for casuals. You should never enter a rate that already includes casual loading into a calculator; instead, check the box for casual loading to have it added automatically.

faqs.q: Is superannuation included in my hourly rate or paid on top?
faqs.a: Super is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. So if your annual salary is $95,000, your employer pays an extra $11,400 into your super fund. This is not part of your take-home pay but is real retirement savings.

faqs.q: How do I compare a salary offer that includes super with one that doesn't?
faqs.a: A total remuneration package (TRP) includes super inside it, while a base salary has super paid on top. To compare, divide the TRP by 1.12 (for 12% super) to get the taxable salary. For example, a $105,000 package is actually $93,750 in salary, which after tax gives less take-home than a $95,000 base salary. Always convert both offers to the same basis before comparing.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Hourly to Annual: The Basics

Whether you're negotiating a new role or just curious about your earning potential, converting an hourly rate to an annual salary is straightforward. The formula is simple: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. For a full-time employee working the standard 38-hour week, that means multiplying your hourly rate by 1,976 hours per year.

This calculation assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. It's a starting point for comparing offers or understanding your gross income before tax and super.

## The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the national minimum wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours, as set by the Fair Work Commission. This is the base rate for employees not covered by an award or agreement. Most workers, however, are covered by a modern award, which may set higher minimum rates, allowances, and penalty rates. You can check the specific rates for your industry using the Modern Awards Pay Database.

For casual employees, a 25% loading is added on top of the base rate. So the casual national minimum wage is $33.05 per hour. This loading compensates for the lack of paid leave entitlements like annual leave and sick leave.

## Casual Loading and Super Paid on Top

Two common points of confusion are casual loading and superannuation. Casual loading is an extra percentage added to your base rate – never enter a rate that already includes casual loading into a calculator. Instead, use a tool that lets you check a box to add it. Superannuation, on the other hand, is paid **on top** of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. This means if your annual salary is $95,000, your employer contributes an extra $11,400 to your super fund, separate from your take-home pay.

## The Fortnightly View

Many people are paid fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, multiply your weekly pay by two. For a full-time employee on the national minimum wage, that's $1,004.90 × 2 = $2,009.80 per fortnight. After tax and Medicare, the take-home amount will be lower. For a detailed breakdown, you can use [the timesheet](/) to enter your hourly rate and see the annual, monthly, fortnightly, and weekly figures.

## Comparing Salary Offers: The Karl Stefanovic Salary Example

You might have heard the phrase "karl stefanovic salary" in headlines – the actual figure is not publicly confirmed, but the principles of comparing offers apply to any income level. When you see a salary advertised, check whether it's a base salary (super paid on top) or a total remuneration package (super included). A common trap is comparing a $95,000 base salary against a $105,000 package. The package, after removing 12% super, is actually a $93,750 salary. After tax, the $95,000 base gives you $74,080 take-home, while the $105,000 package gives only $73,230 – $850 less per year, as shown by the Salary Comparison Calculator.

Always convert both offers to the same basis before deciding. Use [pay guides](/blog) to check award rates, or [reference tables](/data) for tax and super thresholds.

## Tax and Take-Home Pay

For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a 2% Medicare levy (unless you qualify for a reduction). These rates apply to your taxable income, which is your gross salary minus any deductions. For a quick estimate, use [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator.

## When Hours Differ

If you're comparing a role that requires 50 hours per week against one that requires 38, the hourly rate tells a different story. A $100,000 salary for 50 hours gives $38.46 per hour gross, while a $90,000 salary for 38 hours gives $45.55 per hour. The larger salary takes home more cash overall, but the smaller salary pays better per hour. Always factor in the real hours you'll work, not just the contract minimum.

## Super and Packaging

Super is a key part of your total compensation, but it's not spendable until retirement. When comparing offers, look at super beside take-home, not added to it. For more on how salary packaging and super affect your net position, see [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Average Earnings Context

According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics, average weekly earnings for full-time adult ordinary time employees were $2,083.70 in May 2026. That's about $108,352 per year. All employees (including part-time) averaged $1,579.20 per week, or $82,118 per year. These figures give you a benchmark for where your offer sits. See [average pay](/topics/average-pay) for more.

## Final Tips

- Always confirm whether a rate includes casual loading or super.
- Use the national minimum wage as a floor, but check your award for higher rates.
- For a full conversion including tax and super, use [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tools.
- Remember that this is an estimate – your actual pay may vary due to overtime, allowances, or salary sacrifice.

Whether you're earning the minimum wage or a figure like the speculated karl stefanovic salary, the same math applies. Know your hourly rate, your hours, and your entitlements, and you'll be in a strong position to negotiate.
